knowledge:
- key_parameters: data=A dataframe containing the dataset to be plotted ;; x=A string specifying the column name for x-coordinates ;; y=A string specifying the column name for y-coordinates ;; color_by=A string specifying the column name of the factor/grouping variable (referred to as 'factor' in the argument table but 'color_by' in the code) ;; legendTitle=The title of the plot legend ;; pointSize=The size of the ggplot2 points ;; pointAlpha=The transparency level of each point ;; gridSize=An integer defining the precision of the hatched patterns (default is 10000 bins; larger values increase precision but reduce computational efficiency) ;; sparsePoints=A logical vector indicating outlying points, utilizing an internal sparsity detector by default ;; patternList=A list of lists defining custom aesthetics for each pattern (must match the number of groups) ;; colorPalette=A character vector of colors for each group, defaulting to a color-blind friendly palette from dittoSeq
- alternatives: None mentioned in the documentation.
- when_to_use: Use this package when visualizing complex scatterplots (such as spatial transcriptomics or single-cell data) with many distinct groups where color alone is insufficient for clear differentiation or accessibility.
- pitfalls: If patternList is provided, its length must exactly equal the number of groups being plotted. Each sublist within patternList must contain a named element called "pattern" specifying one of the 7 supported pattern types ("-", "|", "/", "\\", "+", "x", or "").

workflows.name: textured_scatterplot
workflows.intent: Create and customize a scatterplot where groups are distinguished by both color and textured hatching patterns.
input: pdacData.csv (a spatial proteomics or coordinate dataset containing X/Y coordinates and group annotations)
workflows.stages: 1. Load the package and prepare the coordinate data with group annotations. 2. Generate a basic scatterHatch plot using default patterns. 3. Define custom pattern aesthetics (angles, line widths, and types) in a list. 4. Generate and render the customized scatterHatch plot.
workflows.code:
library(scatterHatch)

data("pdacData")
pdacData$cellID <- paste0('cell_', 1:nrow(pdacData))
pdacData$Yt <- -pdacData$Yt
pancreas_frames = c(1:6, 27:31, 15:19, 40:44)
PDAC_frames = c(23:26, 35:37, 51:52, 64:65, 77)
small_intestines_frames = c(49:50, 63, 75:76, 88:89, 100:103, 112:116, 125:129, 137:140)
annotateLocation <- function(frame){
    if (frame %in% pancreas_frames){return("Pancreas")}
    if (frame %in% PDAC_frames){return("PDAC")}
    if (frame %in% small_intestines_frames){return("Small Intestine")}
    return("Other")
}
pdacData$location <- sapply(pdacData$frame, annotateLocation)

head(pdacData[, c('Xt', 'Yt', 'location', 'frame')])

plt <- scatterHatch(data = pdacData, x = "Xt", y = "Yt", 
    color_by = "location", legendTitle = "Tissue Type")
plot(plt)

patternList = list(list(pattern="/", angle = 70), list(pattern="-"), list(pattern="x", angle = c(135, 90, 45), lineWidth = 0.2), list(pattern="+"))
plt <- scatterHatch(data = pdacData, x = "Xt", y = "Yt", 
    color_by = "location", legendTitle = "Tissue Type", 
    patternList = patternList)
plot(plt)
